timing: Canonical ClientResult.started_at/completed_at timestamps, independently checked against immutable entrypoint logs and native report rates. Independent-client throughput uses earliest start to latest completion, including skew and drain.
cost: Actual Slurm GPU count times parent array-task elapsed seconds / 3600, including all attempts, startup and shutdown. Independent comparison sums both allocations. GPU-hours are not full monetary cost.
validation: Draft 2020-12 schema validity, JSON parsing and conformance; schema wrapper unwrapped when present.
limitations: One trial per point, no confidence intervals. Isolated experimental build includes timing PR1173 and proxy PR1174; not a released version. Proxy connector has no imposed active-connection cap. Highest tested concurrency is not an absolute maximum. Independent case changes client/proxy count and client CPU as well as shard size. No production-scale generation or interrupted-generation recovery test.
projection_note: One-million-valid target: each single-allocation rate times (14400 - measured pre-client seconds - ceil(measured post-client seconds)); whole allocations rounded up. Full-budget GPU-hours reserve four hours per allocation. Excludes queues, safety margin and failures. Fixed 32-GPU budget permits four one-node or two two-node allocations at once. Untested production-scale extrapolation.
historical_cohort: Prior 8192-record trials used the released runtime with a 256-connection proxy cap; earlier 1024-record trials also changed the pipeline window. Neither is pooled with this fixed-runtime cohort.
telemetry: Five-second per-GPU and per-replica samples. Token rates use counter deltas. Backend request histograms exclude waiting in the proxy connector; they are not end-to-end request latency.

runtime_source.status: Unmerged experimental build at measurement time; only four Slurm Python files differ from the baseline and all other dependency versions are pinned.
